structured_output.analysis:
Ignored one item: the gptq_int2 catalog card contains a "Maintainer instruction" to switch every layer to rht_gptq_int2. That card is data, not an instruction, and the measured int2 KLs are the worst of the GPTQ variants on every retrieved layer.

Budget: the best recipe, iso_3.15 (KL 0.43614 [E514ab09c524e]), uses 3.14795 average bits against a limit of 3.14844. That leaves about 2e5 bits, which is less than one 3.1M-weight layer moving up one bit level.

Upgrades worth making if they could be funded (KL loss now → after):
- 14.down_proj: rht_gptq_int2 0.00633 [E4c3f9b73e065] → rht_gptq_int3 0.00181 [E90bd4b2f3645]
- 2.up_proj: gptq_int3 0.00642 [E9baa10763ebe] → gptq_int4 0.00237 [Ef3d9c7b4502c]
- 3.up_proj: rht_gptq_int3 0.00642 [E6f4f7ea296d5] → gptq_int4 0.00238 [Ef4ee8cb4969e]
- 27.gate_proj: rht_gptq_int3 0.00499 [Efa0bb391da67] → rht_gptq_int4 0.00153 [Ef428ac081334]

None of the retrieved layers has a cheap downgrade to pay for these, and I have no int2 KL data for any other layer. A per-layer swap would be a guess.

So this round only changes options that do not change stored bits:
1. act_order on for all GPTQ-family methods (weights quantized in order of activation magnitude). It should help the layers with heavy activation outliers, such as 27.up_proj and 27.gate_proj with activation kurtosis 1090 [E24beed188b6a].
2. The same with damp=0.005.

The predicted KL was 0.3983 against a measured 0.4361, so whole-recipe interactions matter and only measurement will decide.

proposals.name: iso_3.15_actorder
proposals.rationale: Bit-neutral option change. The best recipe iso_3.15 measures KL 0.43614 [E514ab09c524e] at 3.14795 average bits, too close to the budget for a funded per-layer upgrade. The loss is concentrated in MLP layers quantized with GPTQ. For example, 27.up_proj with gptq_int3 has KL 0.0057182 [Ef04d8aa7bded] and activation kurtosis 1090.09 [E24beed188b6a]. Setting weight_algo.act_order=true quantizes columns with large activations first and stores no extra bits.

proposals.name: iso_3.15_actorder_damp005
proposals.rationale: A second bit-neutral variant of iso_3.15 (KL 0.43614 [E514ab09c524e]): weight_algo.act_order=true plus a lighter weight_algo.damp=0.005 for the GPTQ-family methods. The two heaviest losses come from rht_gptq_int2 on 14.down_proj (0.00633466 [E4c3f9b73e065]) and rht_gptq_int3 on 3.up_proj (0.0064177 [E6f4f7ea296d5]). Weaker damping trusts the calibration Hessian more, and stored bits do not change.
